top.title: Senate summons NCC, MTN, others over dropped calls, airtime deductions
top.description: By Henry Umoru, Abuja The Senate has summoned the Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, and telecommunications operators, including MTN, Airtel, Globacom and T2, over persistent dropped calls, failed connections and unexplained airtime deductions suffered by subscribers. The NCC and telecommunication operators are expected to appear before Senator Aliyu Ikra Bilbis, Zamfara Central-led Senate Committee on Communications. The Committee was mandated to invite the Nigerian Communications Commission and telecommunications operators to investigate complaints of airtime deductions for failed calls, dropped calls, prematurely terminated conversations and inflated charges. The committee is also expected to establish the financial losses suffered by subscribers and report back to the Senate within four weeks, with recommendations for further legislative and regulatory action. The resolution of the Senate on Wednesday was a sequel to a motion titled “Need to curb unjustified deductions from subscribers’ airtime resulting from substandard telecommunications services through robust consumer protection.” The motion was sponsored by the Senate Chief Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno, APC, Borno North. Senator Ned Nwoko, APC, Delta North, who seconded the motion, described the proposal as a straightforward consumer-protection intervention, insisting that the problem affects virtually every Nigerian who relies on telecommunications services. He lamented the contrast between the quality of telephone services in Nigeria and the seamless connectivity experienced in other countries. Presenting the motion on behalf of Monguno, the Deputy Majority Leader, Senator Lola Ashiru, APC, Kwara South, expressed concerns over consumers being charged for calls that were never successfully completed, with lawmakers demanding accountability, refunds and improved quality of service across the telecommunications industry. According to the Senate, for millions of Nigerians, making a telephone call has increasingly become an expensive gamble, just as poor network connectivity, dropped calls, interrupted conversations and failed connections have become recurring complaints among subscribers, many of whom lose airtime even when calls are not successfully completed. Senators warned that Nigerians should not be made to pay for telecommunications services that have not been effectively delivered. They noted that subscribers are frequently compelled to redial numbers several times before establishing a connection, resulting in additional airtime deductions and financial losses, particularly for low-income earners, traders, students and small business owners. The Senate argued that while network challenges may sometimes be unavoidable, consumers should not bear the financial consequences of service failures beyond their control. top.title: The Promise And The Proof
top.description: Tinubu is asking for time to complete his reforms. His challengers must explain how they would deliver better results. The most consequential promise from today’s campaign platform concerns something Nigerians can judge without a political analyst: whether the lights stay on. Speaking at the APC rally in Dutse, President Bola Tinubu promised reliable electricity, lower living costs, support for smaller businesses and more jobs if re-elected. These commitments reach directly into the daily calculations of households and enterprises. For the tailor buying fuel, the graduate searching for work and the family stretching its food budget, the question is immediate: how soon will improvement arrive? That question now sits at the centre of Tinubu’s re-election argument. The APC unveiled its second-term manifesto today, defending the administration’s reforms while promising improvements in security, living standards, infrastructure and governance. The campaign is asking Nigerians to connect the disruption of the present with the prospect of a more prosperous future. It is a politically demanding request. Voters must decide whether the government has established a credible foundation for improvement and whether their experience gives them sufficient reason to renew its mandate. A New Manifesto Meets An Existing Record An incumbent’s manifesto arrives with a companion document: the record of the government seeking another term. The APC’s new commitments include additional electricity meters, wider health insurance coverage and a reduction in the number of out-of-school children. Its presentation also promised identifiable delivery responsibilities and public reporting of progress. These are campaign commitments, whose implementation remains to be demonstrated. That creates an opportunity for a more useful election debate. On electricity, candidates should explain how proposed investments would improve supply to homes and businesses. On employment, they should distinguish training places, temporary opportunities and sustained paid work. On education, they should explain how children will enter school, remain there and learn. The opposition has a responsibility here too. Criticism of government performance becomes more persuasive when accompanied by a workable alternative. A promise to make life affordable needs an explanation of costs, funding and consequences. A promise to improve security needs an account of personnel, intelligence, accountability and protection for affected communities. The campaign can now be judged against specific proposals. top.title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval for $7.7bn external borrowing plan in 2026 budget
top.description: By GiftChapiOdekina, Abuja President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has written to the House of Representatives, seeking legislative approval for the implementation of the N10.79 trillion ($7.7 billion) external borrowing component of the 2026 Appropriation Act. The request, contained in a letter addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, seeks approval to raise $7.707 billion at the budget exchange rate of N1,400 to the dollar to finance part of the Federal Government’s budget deficit. However, the President clarified that the request does not constitute a fresh borrowing plan, explaining that the National Assembly had already approved the amount and made provision for it in the 2026 Appropriation Act. According to him, the current request is aimed at fulfilling the statutory requirements of Sections 21(1) and 27(1) of the Debt Management Office (DMO) Establishment Act, 2003, which require parliamentary approval of the terms and conditions governing external loans. Tinubu explained that Section 21(1) prohibits the Minister of Finance from obtaining or approving external loans unless their terms and conditions have been presented to and approved by the National Assembly. He added that Section 27(1) empowers the National Assembly to approve standard terms and conditions for negotiating and accepting external loans and issuing guarantees. The President recalled that the 2026 Appropriation Act provided for N29.218 trillion in new borrowings to finance the budget deficit, comprising N18.28 trillion in domestic borrowing and N10.79 trillion in external borrowing. He said the Federal Government would pursue multiple financing options simultaneously, taking into consideration their costs, benefits and the time required to access the funds. Tinubu, however, indicated that greater emphasis would be placed on Eurobond issuance, which he said could be concluded more quickly and provide access to larger amounts of financing at relatively lower costs. On the proposed Eurobond issuance, the President noted that the final terms and conditions would be determined at the time of pricing, depending on prevailing market conditions. He assured that the Federal Ministry of Finance and the Debt Management Office would work to secure the most favourable terms available in the international market. According to the letter, the external borrowing is intended to finance projects and programmes captured in the 2026 budget, particularly in priority sectors including defence and security, transportation, agriculture, power, education and health. Tinubu said the borrowing would also support the administration’s efforts to stabilise and strengthen ongoing macroeconomic reforms. He further argued that the proceeds would contribute to the country’s external reserves, as the funds would be received by the Central Bank of Nigeria on behalf of the Federal Government, thereby supporting the naira exchange rate. top.title: Joe Lacob talks Juste Jocyte’s future after Natalie Nakase drama
top.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Golden State Valkyries owner Joe Lacob isn’t shutting the door on Juste Jocyte. Juste Jocyte didn’t bite her tongue after spending basically the entire WNBA Finals glued to the pine, seeing just six total minutes on the floor. The 20-year-old made her feelings known in an interview with the Lithuanian media, making it clear she was miserable with how Natalie Nakase used her. Now, heading into the offseason, Jocyte is putting the Valkyries front office on notice, telling them she has zero interest in riding the bench next year, and she won’t stick around without real minutes. Joe Lacob issues an update on Juste Jocyte’s future Joe Lacob is trying to play damage control before the situation spirals. Instead of taking the bait and firing back at Jocyte’s comments, the Valkyries owner is playing the long game, making it clear he doesn’t want to let the 20-year-old walk away. He said: “I kind of understand she’s competitive and would like to win and didn’t play. But she’s also only 20. We had a pretty great roster, very deep. I think she can be a very good player and we’d really love to have her back. “So I think she will certainly earn a lot more playing time in the future. She didn’t get to play as much as she wanted to, and that’s understandable. “I think she can be a very good player and we would really love to have her back.” Even with Lacob trying to play nice, it’s hard to picture Jocyte sticking around in the Bay. That bridge with Nakase is burned, and Golden State isn’t about to let locker room bad blood poison the culture they’re building. Once trust is shot, a clean break is the only realistic way out. top.title: MCC to introduce Spirit of Cricket Award at ILT20 Season 5
top.description: The Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) will introduce a Spirit of Cricket Award at the ILT20 Season 5, recognising a team or individual who best reflects the game's values during the tournament, which begins in the UAE on November 21. The award will be presented at the end of the competition on December 20, marking the first such recognition at the six-team T20 league. MCC, the guardian of cricket's Laws, will work with the tournament organisers to promote sportsmanship and fair play among players. The partnership is part of MCC's wider effort to promote the Spirit of Cricket across the game. The Club has previously worked with ICC Europe to present similar awards at three men's sub-regional World Cup qualification events earlier this year. Rob Lynch, MCC's Director of Cricket and Operations, said franchise leagues could play an important role in setting standards for player behaviour. “MCC sees franchise leagues as the standard-bearers for playing the game in the right way – playing hard but playing fair and with a smile on your face,” Lynch said. He added that the competitive nature of franchise cricket, where international team-mates often face each other, could help improve conduct across the sport. Mike Fordham, Interim Chief Operating Officer of the ILT20, said the partnership aligned with the league's emphasis on sporting values. He also pointed to the participation of players from 19 cricketing nations across its six franchises this season. “The tournament has always been hugely competitive with top quality cricket on display. Our matches have always been played in the right spirit with cricket’s traditional sporting values remaining at the forefront,” Fordham said. Season 5 will run from November 21 to December 20, with matches scheduled at the Sheikh Zayed Cricket Stadium in Abu Dhabi, Dubai International Stadium and Sharjah Cricket Stadium. Defending champions Desert Vipers will be joined by Gulf Giants, MI Emirates, Dubai Capitals, Abu Dhabi Knight Riders and Sharjah Warriorz in the 34-match competition. Previous winners include Gulf Giants, MI Emirates and Dubai Capitals. The new recognition will be separate from the main MCC Spirit of Cricket Award, established by MCC and the BBC in 2013 in honour of Christopher Martin-Jenkins.

top.title: Robert Horry Rips Walker Kessler’s Offensive Game: “Guys In Elementary Got Better Post Moves Than Him”
top.description: Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers have the NBA’s best record at 10-2, and new arrival Walker Kessler has played his part in their early success. Kessler has impressed on defense, and former Laker Robert Horry likes what he has seen from the big man on that end of the floor. What Horry, who won three titles with the Lakers, doesn’t like, though, is Kessler’s offensive game, and he urged him to improve on the Big Shot Bob Podcast . “You know what’s really scary about Walker Kessler?” Horry said. “Hey, I know guys in elementary got better post moves than him. He got no post moves, man. I’m like, who is teaching this dude any post moves? You’re seven f***ing feet tall. Get you a little jump hook, man. You don’t have to dunk everything.” Kessler really doesn’t have a reliable post move. The 25-year-old is primarily a rim-runner, and if you are good at that next to Luka Doncic , you’ll score some points. Kessler is averaging 14.9 points, 10.8 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 1.3 steals, and 2.3 blocks per game for the Lakers in 2026-27. Over 60 percent of his field goal attempts have been within three feet of the basket, and only 1.8 percent have come from beyond 10 feet. Now, Kessler showed off some range in the 2025-26 season for the Utah Jazz . He went 6-8 from three in five games before needing season-ending shoulder surgery. So, when the Lakers acquired Kessler, the No. 22 pick in the 2022 NBA Draft, from the Jazz in the summer, the expectation was that he’d be a threat from beyond the arc. He even shared that head coach JJ Redick wanted him to shoot more threes , but he hasn’t even attempted a single one through 12 games. “I don’t even think he wants to score ’cause I’ve seen him get offensive rebounds and kick that b***h out instead of crunching that b***h,” Horry said. “… I’m like, dude, you 7 ft tall. Get you a power dribble. Go up and dunk that b***h too. Like [Shaquille O’Neal], you monkey dunk that b***h. That’s what he said. That’s what Shaq used to say. So dunk on somebody and then just move on. “That’s what I want him to do and stop kicking that b***h out ’cause you don’t get no plays ran for you,” Horry added. Now, teams like the player who gets the offensive rebound to kick it out for an open three. That could well be the case here, but we don’t know for sure. While Kessler isn’t the perfect offensive center, that wasn’t why the Lakers gave him a four-year, $130 million contract and gave up two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps to the Jazz. They wanted a rim runner and a defensive anchor, and he is just that. “He’s a great shot blocker,” Horry said. “And the thing I like about Kessler the best is he goes after everything. And even though he’s gotten dunked on a couple times, he don’t give a s***… He’s still going to go out and try to block. top.title: Top 2027 recruit Amaya Manuel commits to Tennessee
top.description: Top 2027 recruit Amaya Manuel has committed to Tennessee , she announced. The 5-8 point guard from Saint Louis (MO) Lift For Life Academy chose the Lady Vols over programs including Missouri and Arkansas. “Definitely a family type of environment,” she previously told Rivals of factors she was considering. “I want to do a lot of team bonding and stuff. top.title: JJ Gabriel set to sign Real Madrid contract by early next week – report
top.description: JJ Gabriel set to sign Real Madrid contract by early next week – report Real Madrid are expected to complete the signing of Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel by the beginning of next week, with the 16-year-old’s move to the Spanish capital approaching its final stages. According to journalist Ben Fernandes Santos , the agreement is close to being finalised, with the teenager having made his preference clear to the European clubs interested in securing his signature. It is to be noted that Gabriel attracted attention across Europe following his decision to leave Manchester United in September. Real Madrid, after tough negotiations and a fight with other suitors, emerged as his preferred destination, with Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain among the clubs previously linked with the highly-rated forward. Manchester United fail to convince JJ Gabriel to stay Manchester United reportedly made several attempts to change Gabriel’s mind, with club executives and manager Michael Carrick holding discussions with the player and his representatives. The teenager requested to leave United in September and has since been training independently in Spain while his future is being resolved. His decision became clearer when he was asked to choose between Barcelona and Real Madrid . “Obviously, Real Madrid,” he said. As reported before, Real Madrid had reached a verbal agreement with the teenager and were confident of signing him. However, formal club-to-club negotiations had not yet taken place until a few weeks back. Real Madrid have a clear development plan Real Madrid have won the race for JJ Gabriel. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) Real Madrid are understood to want Gabriel to begin his development with Castilla , allowing him to experience senior football while remaining close to the first-team environment. The Spanish club believe their pathway offers an attractive opportunity for the teenager to progress towards the senior squad. His representative, Ali Barat, has been involved in discussions over the move, while reports have also suggested that Jose Mourinho played a role in convincing Gabriel that Madrid would be the right destination. top.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
top.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. top.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
top.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. top.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
top.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. top.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
top.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. nigeria.title: Senate summons NCC, MTN, others over dropped calls, airtime deductions
nigeria.description: By Henry Umoru, Abuja The Senate has summoned the Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, and telecommunications operators, including MTN, Airtel, Globacom and T2, over persistent dropped calls, failed connections and unexplained airtime deductions suffered by subscribers. The NCC and telecommunication operators are expected to appear before Senator Aliyu Ikra Bilbis, Zamfara Central-led Senate Committee on Communications. The Committee was mandated to invite the Nigerian Communications Commission and telecommunications operators to investigate complaints of airtime deductions for failed calls, dropped calls, prematurely terminated conversations and inflated charges. The committee is also expected to establish the financial losses suffered by subscribers and report back to the Senate within four weeks, with recommendations for further legislative and regulatory action. The resolution of the Senate on Wednesday was a sequel to a motion titled “Need to curb unjustified deductions from subscribers’ airtime resulting from substandard telecommunications services through robust consumer protection.” The motion was sponsored by the Senate Chief Whip, Senator Mohammed Tahir Monguno, APC, Borno North. Senator Ned Nwoko, APC, Delta North, who seconded the motion, described the proposal as a straightforward consumer-protection intervention, insisting that the problem affects virtually every Nigerian who relies on telecommunications services. He lamented the contrast between the quality of telephone services in Nigeria and the seamless connectivity experienced in other countries. Presenting the motion on behalf of Monguno, the Deputy Majority Leader, Senator Lola Ashiru, APC, Kwara South, expressed concerns over consumers being charged for calls that were never successfully completed, with lawmakers demanding accountability, refunds and improved quality of service across the telecommunications industry. According to the Senate, for millions of Nigerians, making a telephone call has increasingly become an expensive gamble, just as poor network connectivity, dropped calls, interrupted conversations and failed connections have become recurring complaints among subscribers, many of whom lose airtime even when calls are not successfully completed. Senators warned that Nigerians should not be made to pay for telecommunications services that have not been effectively delivered. They noted that subscribers are frequently compelled to redial numbers several times before establishing a connection, resulting in additional airtime deductions and financial losses, particularly for low-income earners, traders, students and small business owners. The Senate argued that while network challenges may sometimes be unavoidable, consumers should not bear the financial consequences of service failures beyond their control. nigeria.title: The Promise And The Proof
nigeria.description: Tinubu is asking for time to complete his reforms. His challengers must explain how they would deliver better results. The most consequential promise from today’s campaign platform concerns something Nigerians can judge without a political analyst: whether the lights stay on. Speaking at the APC rally in Dutse, President Bola Tinubu promised reliable electricity, lower living costs, support for smaller businesses and more jobs if re-elected. These commitments reach directly into the daily calculations of households and enterprises. For the tailor buying fuel, the graduate searching for work and the family stretching its food budget, the question is immediate: how soon will improvement arrive? That question now sits at the centre of Tinubu’s re-election argument. The APC unveiled its second-term manifesto today, defending the administration’s reforms while promising improvements in security, living standards, infrastructure and governance. The campaign is asking Nigerians to connect the disruption of the present with the prospect of a more prosperous future. It is a politically demanding request. Voters must decide whether the government has established a credible foundation for improvement and whether their experience gives them sufficient reason to renew its mandate. A New Manifesto Meets An Existing Record An incumbent’s manifesto arrives with a companion document: the record of the government seeking another term. The APC’s new commitments include additional electricity meters, wider health insurance coverage and a reduction in the number of out-of-school children. Its presentation also promised identifiable delivery responsibilities and public reporting of progress. These are campaign commitments, whose implementation remains to be demonstrated. That creates an opportunity for a more useful election debate. On electricity, candidates should explain how proposed investments would improve supply to homes and businesses. On employment, they should distinguish training places, temporary opportunities and sustained paid work. On education, they should explain how children will enter school, remain there and learn. The opposition has a responsibility here too. Criticism of government performance becomes more persuasive when accompanied by a workable alternative. A promise to make life affordable needs an explanation of costs, funding and consequences. A promise to improve security needs an account of personnel, intelligence, accountability and protection for affected communities. The campaign can now be judged against specific proposals. Nigerians should expect the candidates to defend them. nigeria.title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval for $7.7bn external borrowing plan in 2026 budget
nigeria.description: By GiftChapiOdekina, Abuja President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has written to the House of Representatives, seeking legislative approval for the implementation of the N10.79 trillion ($7.7 billion) external borrowing component of the 2026 Appropriation Act. The request, contained in a letter addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, seeks approval to raise $7.707 billion at the budget exchange rate of N1,400 to the dollar to finance part of the Federal Government’s budget deficit. However, the President clarified that the request does not constitute a fresh borrowing plan, explaining that the National Assembly had already approved the amount and made provision for it in the 2026 Appropriation Act. According to him, the current request is aimed at fulfilling the statutory requirements of Sections 21(1) and 27(1) of the Debt Management Office (DMO) Establishment Act, 2003, which require parliamentary approval of the terms and conditions governing external loans. Tinubu explained that Section 21(1) prohibits the Minister of Finance from obtaining or approving external loans unless their terms and conditions have been presented to and approved by the National Assembly. He added that Section 27(1) empowers the National Assembly to approve standard terms and conditions for negotiating and accepting external loans and issuing guarantees. The President recalled that the 2026 Appropriation Act provided for N29.218 trillion in new borrowings to finance the budget deficit, comprising N18.28 trillion in domestic borrowing and N10.79 trillion in external borrowing. He said the Federal Government would pursue multiple financing options simultaneously, taking into consideration their costs, benefits and the time required to access the funds. Tinubu, however, indicated that greater emphasis would be placed on Eurobond issuance, which he said could be concluded more quickly and provide access to larger amounts of financing at relatively lower costs. On the proposed Eurobond issuance, the President noted that the final terms and conditions would be determined at the time of pricing, depending on prevailing market conditions. He assured that the Federal Ministry of Finance and the Debt Management Office would work to secure the most favourable terms available in the international market. According to the letter, the external borrowing is intended to finance projects and programmes captured in the 2026 budget, particularly in priority sectors including defence and security, transportation, agriculture, power, education and health. Tinubu said the borrowing would also support the administration’s efforts to stabilise and strengthen ongoing macroeconomic reforms. He further argued that the proceeds would contribute to the country’s external reserves, as the funds would be received by the Central Bank of Nigeria on behalf of the Federal Government, thereby supporting the naira exchange rate. nigeria.title: Otti urges lawyers to defend rights of vulnerable Nigerians
nigeria.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has urged legal practitioners across the country to prioritise access to justice by extending legal services to indigent and vulnerable citizens who cannot afford legal representation. Otti made the call in Umuahia while declaring open the 2026 Nigerian Bar Association Section on Public Interest and Development Law (NBA-SPIDEL) Annual Conference, with the theme, “In Public Interest: Advancing Justice, Democracy and Development.” The governor urged lawyers to adopt a more humane approach to cases involving indigent and vulnerable citizens, stressing that the pursuit of justice should take precedence over professional interests and financial considerations. He said the legal profession had a responsibility to provide assistance to people who lacked the financial capacity to defend their rights. “And because you are lawyers, we need to go the extra mile of asking ourselves, beyond all the things that have been said, how can we be of service to people who cannot pay? “How can we be of service to the vulnerable? How can we help people who on their own cannot afford to help themselves? “Until government gets to that level, we have not cracked the surface. If it is only about you and then the money you make and all that, then you don’t need to be here. You may as well go and do something else,” he said. Otti said his administration had discovered cases of people who remained in correctional facilities despite allegedly having committed no offences warranting their continued detention. He cited the case of an individual who was allegedly detained for supporting an opposition political party, adding that the experience prompted him to direct the Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice to work with the Chief Judge to secure the release of such inmates. The governor also warned against the misuse of the justice system to punish citizens for expressing their opinions or engaging in activities on social media, insisting that the protection of individual rights must remain central to governance. On judicial infrastructure, Otti disclosed that his administration would soon commission 10 newly constructed courthouses equipped with renewable energy systems, digitalised court records and broadband connectivity. He also urged lawyers to embrace technological advancements and prepare for emerging changes in legal practice. In his keynote address, former Vice President, Prof. Yemi Osinbajo, urged lawyers to move beyond litigation and legal interpretation to champion public interest, protect disadvantaged citizens and ensure that democracy delivers tangible benefits to the people. nigeria.title: 17 rescued, one injured as CNG commercial bus explodes on Lagos–Ibadan Expressway
nigeria.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni At least ​17 people, including a driver, were rescued unhurt on Wednesday after a Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)-powered commercial bus burst into flames following a gas explosion at Berger Bus Stop along the Lagos-bound section of the Lagos–Ibadan Expressway. ​One male passenger, who was seated at the rear of the fully loaded Hiace bus (registration number EKY 798 YK), sustained severe burn injuries and was rushed to the Lagos State Trauma and Emergency Centre at Toll Gate for urgent medical attention. ​According to eyewitnesses, the vehicle was conveying 18 occupants from the Mowe-Ibafo axis toward Lagos when it erupted into flames, triggering panic among passengers and motorists. Commenting on the accident, Lagos State Traffic Management Authority, LASTMA General Manager, Olalekan Bakare-Oki, through Director of Public Affairs and Enlightenment, Adebayo Taofiq, LASTMA personnel promptly mobilised to the scene to evacuate the occupants, while officers of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service extinguished the blaze to prevent it from spreading. Personnel from the Ojodu Police Division also provided security and maintained order throughout the rescue and firefighting operations. ​Commending the operation, Bakare-Oki praised the agency’s personnel for their swift intervention and thanked the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service and the Nigeria Police Force for their collaboration. ​He noted that the incident underscores the importance of rapid emergency response and inter-agency synergy in mitigating road disasters. Bakare-Oki therefore urged commercial transport operators—particularly those running CNG-powered vehicles—to prioritise regular professional inspections, adhere to safety standards, and ensure the proper maintenance of their gas storage and delivery systems. nigeria.title: Gov Yusuf presents N1.107trn 2027 budget, earmarks 63% for capital projects
nigeria.description: Sekinat Osundiji Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has presented a proposed budget of N1.107 trillion for the 2027 fiscal year to the state House of Assembly. The budget, tagged “Budget of Consolidating Gains and Accelerated Rural Development,” is the fourth and final budget of the administration’s first tenure, which is expected to end on May 29, 2027. Presenting the estimates, Yusuf said the budget was designed to consolidate existing achievements, accelerate rural development and ensure the completion of ongoing projects before the expiration of his administration’s first term. The governor said his administration had achieved more than 90 per cent of the programmes, projects and policies outlined in its development blueprint. He, however, acknowledged that some commitments remained outstanding, adding that the 2027 budget would prioritise their completion, alongside strengthening essential public services. “This is not merely nominal. It is a fiscal commitment to ensure that no ongoing project is abandoned,” he said. He added that the budget would consolidate reforms in free education, primary healthcare revitalisation and urban renewal, while ensuring that residents benefit from government projects and programmes. Yusuf said the proposed budget would focus on education, healthcare, infrastructure, agriculture, water supply and human capital development, which he described as central to improving productivity and living conditions in the state. Budget breakdown Giving a breakdown of the proposed expenditure, the governor said ₦693.47 billion was earmarked for capital expenditure, while ₦413.55 billion was allocated to recurrent expenditure. He said the proposed capital-to-recurrent expenditure ratio was 63 per cent to 37 per cent, reflecting the administration’s intention to direct more resources towards infrastructure and other development projects while meeting its recurrent obligations. On revenue projections, Yusuf put the state’s total recurrent revenue at ₦692.64 billion, comprising ₦142.84 billion from internally generated revenue and revenue from the Federation Account. He said the projected recurrent revenue represented a 34 per cent decrease compared with the 2026 fiscal year. However, he projected a 73 per cent increase in internally generated revenue, attributing the growth to reforms at the Kano State Internal Revenue Service, including digital revenue administration and the expansion of the Easy Tax digitisation initiative. The governor further said the state expected ₦354.38 billion in capital receipts from grants and loans, alongside an opening balance of ₦60 billion to finance the proposed budget. He said the allocations would support projects and programmes across the state’s economic and social sectors. Yusuf added that the government would prioritise completing ongoing projects and strengthening existing programmes before the end of its first tenure in May 2027. nigeria.description: Manchester United have reportedly reached a “verbal agreement in principle” with Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick as their manager in a bid to revive the fortunes of the struggling English giants. Carrick’s position at Old Trafford has been the subject of intense speculation following United’s worst start to a season in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run. He remains in post but it is believed Carrick’s future will be decided at a meeting attended by influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox in Monaco on Wednesday. Berrada and Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick. United States head coach Pochettino has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea. It was only three months ago, however, that Pochettino signed a contract extension to remain with the United States through to the 2030 World Cup. US Soccer would be due compensation should he move to Manchester, with the 54-year-old understood to have a $10 million (£7.5 million) release clause. But United were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down. It appeared former United and England midfielder Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed Aston Villa by two goals on Sunday. When United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it was interpreted as a positive sign for Carrick as the players were still fighting for him. But a change now appears likely, with former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe, ex-Chelsea chief Antonio Conte and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann also linked with the United job. nigeria.title: Prison Break actor Stacy Keach dies at 85
nigeria.description: American actor Stacy Keach, renowned for his roles in television and film productions spanning more than six decades, has died at the age of 85. Keach died on Tuesday at his home in Magdalenka, Poland, following a prolonged battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure. His wife, Małgosia Tomassi Keach, announced his death in a statement, describing him as a courageous fighter whose resilience defined both his personal life and acting career. “It is with profound sadness and a broken heart that I announce the passing of my darling husband, Stacy Keach. After a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure, Stacy peacefully departed this world,” she said. She described the late actor as a legendary performer whose work earned him admiration from audiences worldwide, adding that his death had left an immeasurable void in the family. Keach began his acting career on Broadway in the 1960s before transitioning to film in the 1970s. He gained recognition for his performance alongside Faye Dunaway in the 1971 film Doc. He became particularly popular for portraying private investigator Mike Hammer in several television productions, including Mickey Spillane’s Mike Hammer and The New Mike Hammer. His other notable screen appearances included the television series Prison Break, Blue Bloods and Titus, as well as films such as The Long Riders, Nebraska and The Bourne Legacy. The actor also appeared in the biblical miniseries Jesus of Nazareth, where he portrayed Barabbas. Over a career spanning approximately 60 years, Keach accumulated more than 200 film and television credits and earned recognition as an accomplished interpreter of Shakespeare. His career also included stage performances and a Tony Award nomination, further establishing his reputation as a versatile actor. Keach came from a family with strong ties to the entertainment industry. His father, Stacy Keach Sr., was a respected actor, while his brother, James Keach, is also an actor and filmmaker. He was previously reported to have suffered a heart attack on stage in Chicago in 2017. Keach is survived by his wife, Małgosia, their children, Karolina and Shannon, grandchildren and other members of the extended family. In her tribute, his wife said his unforgettable voice, remarkable spirit and love for his family would remain with them forever. nigeria.title: Liverpool should have had penalty for shirt-pull on Isak – Panel
nigeria.description: Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty for the shirt-pull on Alexander Isak in their Premier League match against Arsenal, an expert panel ruled Wednesday. The Sweden striker’s shirt was tugged by Gunners defender Jurrien Timber in the match at Anfield on November 1, which Premier League champions Arsenal won 1-0. Referee Andy Madley let the incident pass without sanction, and video assistant referee Stuart Attwell decided against recommending a review. The decision was criticised at the time by pundits such as Jamie Carragher and Ian Wright, and now the five-person Key Match Incidents panel has said a penalty should have been awarded. Madley’s decision was criticised by four of the panellists, who felt Timber’s challenge met the threshold for a holding offence, while three felt Attwell should have intervened because it was a clear and obvious error by Madley. Isak did not make any protest about Timber’s shirt-pull to the on-field officials, in a match which was settled by Kai Havertz’s goal for the Gunners. Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola, asked after the match whether Isak should have gone down following the challenge, replied: “It’s a shame you ask me this question, but honestly, yes, we have to tell them (the players), go down, because they (the officials) are not going to call it otherwise. “And then referees complain why they go down. Because if you don’t go down, you don’t call it. Then it’s like, no, you are all the time going down. “But I think Alex is honest. He tries to go for the ball, everyone can see live straight away there is a clear, clear pull.” The post Liverpool should have had penalty for shirt-pull on Isak – Panel appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Nearly 64,000 Nigerians flee to Niger over insecurity – UNHCR
nigeria.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Nearly 64,000 Nigerians have fled their homes and crossed into neighbouring Niger Republic since the beginning of 2026 to escape escalating violence involving Islamist militants and armed criminal gangs, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) has disclosed. The UN refugee agency, in a briefing issued on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, warned that the growing influx was creating a deepening humanitarian and protection crisis in Niger, which is already hosting more than 500,000 refugees and asylum-seekers. According to UNHCR, approximately 327,500 Nigerians are already seeking refuge in Niger, while several hundred others have reportedly crossed into neighbouring Benin Republic because of worsening insecurity in northern Nigeria. The agency’s Director of External Relations, Dominique Hyde, said most of the newly arrived Nigerians had settled in the border regions of Diffa, in southeastern Niger, and Tahoua, in the western part of the country. In October alone, about 1,200 Nigerians crossed into Diffa, while another 3,400 arrived in Tahoua. UNHCR disclosed that more than 23,000 people, over two-thirds of them children, had arrived in Diffa since the beginning of the year. The agency expressed concern over the difficult conditions facing the displaced families, many of whom are living in makeshift shelters without adequate food, clean drinking water, healthcare and other essential services. It said some women were forced to walk several kilometres daily to fetch water for their families, while humanitarian organisations had reported increasing cases of malnutrition, respiratory infections and poor sanitation among the new arrivals. The refugee agency also raised concerns over the registration of displaced Nigerians, revealing that only about five per cent of those who arrived in Niger this year had been formally registered. The absence of proper documentation, it warned, was making it difficult for thousands of refugees to access humanitarian assistance and essential public services. The situation is further complicated by insecurity and climate-related challenges in Niger, particularly in the Diffa region, where more than 70 per cent of the country’s reported security incidents this year have occurred. Despite the growing humanitarian pressure, UNHCR acknowledged the support provided by Niger’s authorities and host communities, including the allocation of land for temporary shelters. The agency, however, appealed for increased international assistance, seeking $11.4 million to expand its humanitarian response in Niger, Nigeria and Benin. The appeal includes $2 million for immediate critical interventions covering food, water, shelter, healthcare, refugee registration and protection. UNHCR warned that without additional funding, thousands of vulnerable families fleeing violence could be left without essential humanitarian assistance. nigeria.description: …..As Solus, Olusosun dumpsites resume operations …PSPs to deploy over 700 trucks By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has warned Private Sector Participation (PSP) waste operators to deliver immediate results or face enforcement measures, following the reopening of the Solus and Olusosun dumpsites after months of closure. nigeria.title: Police probe Blord over armed officers’ escort
nigeria.description: The Nigeria Police Force has launched an investigation into a viral video showing armed police officers escorting businessman Linus Williams, popularly known as Blord, at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Enugu. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, described the deployment of the officers as “unlawful and illegal”, saying an investigation had commenced into the incident. Iniedu disclosed this in a statement posted on his official X account on Wednesday while reacting to the video. “Unlawful and illegal. Investigation has commenced into this incident please. We say #notoimpunity,” he wrote. The video, which Blord shared on his Instagram page on Tuesday, showed him arriving at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport in Enugu, accompanied by armed police officers dressed in camouflage uniforms and tactical gear. The businessman was seen wearing a red-and-white striped traditional cap associated with the Kwankwaso political brand. He was also seen arriving in a black Cadillac with the personalised number plate, “B-LORD”. Other scenes in the footage showed Blord walking alongside the armed officers at the airport and at other locations, including what appeared to be his business premises. The officers were seen providing him with an escort and opening the vehicle door for him. Captioning the video, Blord wrote: “Back to base, business as usual. From the airport to a brief stop at BlordGroup Enugu branch, then back to Awka. Every move has its purpose, and the vision never takes a break. Blord is home!” In another Instagram post, the businessman said he had been in Sabon Gari, Kano State, where he met his “brothers” before returning to Enugu. The development comes months after President Bola Tinubu ordered the withdrawal of police officers attached to Very Important Persons (VIPs) across the country and their redeployment to core policing duties. Tinubu gave the directive at a security meeting with service chiefs and the Director-General of the Department of State Services in Abuja on November 23, 2025. According to a statement by the President’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, VIPs requiring protection would henceforth be assigned armed operatives of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps instead of police officers. The President said the measure was aimed at strengthening police presence in communities, particularly those facing security challenges. On December 6, 2025, the police also deployed a Special Enforcement Team to monitor compliance with the directive, beginning with an operation in Lagos. The then Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Benjamin Hundeyin, said the exercise recorded no cases of unauthorised deployment of police escorts. nigeria.title: Govt Scared of Peter Obi’s Popularity, Campaign Camp Pushes Back Over Flamingos Airport Encounter
nigeria.description: Representatives of Peter Obi have dismissed accusations that the presidential candidate was “playing to the gallery” during a recent encounter with Nigeria’s national U-17 women’s football team, the Flamingos, at the airport. Addressing criticism from political opponents and government commentators, a representative for Obi’s camp said the incident was a spontaneous moment during routine domestic travel, claiming federal officials and the ruling party are unsettled by the opposition leader’s widespread public support. ‘A Man on the Move’ Rebutting claims that the airport greeting was a staged publicity stunt, Obi’s campaign team clarified that the candidate was at the airport to board a commercial flight for scheduled engagements across the country when he crossed paths with the victorious sports delegation. “I don’t understand what they mean by our candidate playing to the gallery,” the spokesperson said. “Every Nigerian knows that Peter Obi is a man on the move. He has engagements across the country, and at that time, he was at the airport just like any other traveller trying to catch a flight to his next destination.” The statement emphasised that meeting the Flamingos—who were returning from international competition—was entirely coincidental, adding that Obi’s decision to approach the team was an act of national pride. “It just so happened that the Flamingos were there at the same time, and like any patriotic Nigerian, he simply wanted to greet them and congratulate them on their victory.” Pattern of Restrictions The campaign further alleged that this was not an isolated event, asserting that security or administrative barriers have previously been used to prevent Obi from interacting with victorious Nigerian athletes during public appearances. Obi’s camp described the government’s reaction as indicative of political anxiety over his public visibility. “This is not the first time this has happened,” the representative noted. “He has been prevented from greeting victorious Nigerian athletes before. This latest incident just shows how jittery the government is. They do not want him taking the spotlight because wherever Peter Obi goes, Nigerians rally behind him.” ﻿ ﻿ Political Friction Ahead of Elections The clash underscores the heightened sensitivity surrounding public engagements and political optics as major parties structure their national campaigns. While government supporters have accused opposition figures of leveraging national sports achievements for political leverage, Obi’s campaign maintained that public enthusiasm during his travel movements remains organic and unscripted. “While it is understandable that they are scared, it is pathetic, to say the least,” the spokesperson concluded, reiterating that the presidential candidate will continue his scheduled nationwide tours and citizen engagements despite ongoing political scrutiny. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing how people learn, work, communicate and solve problems. In today’s world, if you’re not on board with AI, it could be said you’re being resistant to the fastest-growing technological innovation in the world. From students researching academic subjects to professionals developing business ideas, AI tools have become companions in everyday activities for people. They can help save time, explore new ideas, understand difficult concepts and approach tasks differently. However, as more people embrace these AI tools, it is important to understand that using AI effectively goes beyond knowing what prompts to enter. It requires knowing when to use it, how to question its responses and, most importantly, when to rely on your own knowledge and judgement. AI could make us better at what we do, not make us dependent on it. Here are ways we think you use AI effectively: Use AI as a Research Assistant One of the most effective ways to use AI is for research and information gathering. Whether you are writing an article, preparing a presentation or exploring an unfamiliar subject, AI can help you identify relevant topics, explain complex ideas and suggest areas worth investigating. You can ask it to break down unfamiliar concepts, identify key questions, or suggest research directions. However, do not treat every response as fact. Verify important information using credible sources, published research, books and reliable websites. AI can help you find information, but you are responsible for establishing what is true. Use AI to Brainstorm and Explore Ideas Like knowledge gathering, AI can brainstorm ideas with you. Sometimes, the hardest part of starting a project is knowing where to begin. AI can help you overcome this challenge by suggesting ideas, exploring different approaches and presenting perspectives you may not have considered. For writers, entrepreneurs, researchers and creatives, it can be a useful brainstorming partner. entertainment.title: 5 New Albums to Listen to This Week: Skepta, Phyno, Ty Bello & More

Photo Credit: Skepta/Instagram Your playlist could do with a little shake-up, and these five albums might be exactly what it needs. Skepta is reconnecting with his roots, Phyno is giving us more of the indigenous rap we love, Ty Bello has two albums exploring different expressions of worship, and Anendlessocean and Tobe Nwigwe are taking their sounds in interesting directions. The album features powerhouse collaborations, including Seyi Vibez on the opener “ Ndu Ka Aku ”, Fireboy DML on “ I Believe ”, and Jeriq on “ Ije Enu ”. Whether taking the government to task on “20 Years to Come” or offering uplifting anthems like “ Chukwu Okike ”, Phyno proves why he remains a definitive voice in African hip-hop. ﻿ Ty Bello: I Speak Lion and I Speak Lamb Creative powerhouse Ty Bello delivers a massive double-album listening experience with I Speak Lion and I Speak Lamb . Split into two distinct spiritual volumes, the expansive project captures both the bold, triumphant authority of worship and its quiet, intimate moments. ﻿ I Speak Lion leans into explosive, high-energy sounds designed to spark courage, featuring powerful pairings with Sunmisola Agbebi , Greatman Takit , and Limoblaze . entertainment.description: Africa’s tech icon and Chairman of Zinox Group , Leo Stan Ekeh , has told an international gathering of women leaders that his decision to build a technology company in Africa, at a time when the sector was virtually non-existent on the continent, amounted to what he described as “corporate suicide”. Speaking on the theme “Losing the Fear” , at The International Women Leadership Conference (TIWLC) in Dubai, organised by the Ibukun Awosika Leadership Foundation, Ekeh , who was a keynote speaker on the final day of this year’s conference, addressed over 600 women industry leaders from different countries across the globe. He said he returned from his studies abroad to a Nigeria where his peers were filing into banking, oil and gas, and where technology was largely seen as a foreign game. Ekeh, who studied Economics in India, said he was discouraged from pursuing a postgraduate degree in Computer Science in Europe because of the prevailing perception then that Africa might have little need for computers over the next 35 years, potentially leaving him frustrated. He subsequently opted for a postgraduate degree in Risk Management before pursuing a Master’s degree in Business Law (LLM) at London Guildhall University. He recalled that he could not sit his final law examinations because he had diverted his tuition fees into his passion for technology entrepreneurship. He also disclosed that he had fended off recruitment attempts by international technology companies that had sought to hire him before his return to Africa. “I chose the road not taken,” he told the conference. “It was corporate suicide in the eyes of my parents and many others. I lost the fear because I believed technology was the master key that would unlock possibilities for Nigeria and Africa.” He said the journey came with considerable hardship, including living on one meal a day for over three years and sleeping in a very small room in his office. According to him, his vision was to create a Nigerian and, by extension, an African IT identity. Recalling the launch of his first company, Task Systems Ltd, over 35 years ago, the company that pioneered desktop publishing and computer graphics in Nigeria. sports.title: MCC to introduce Spirit of Cricket Award at ILT20 Season 5
sports.description: The Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) will introduce a Spirit of Cricket Award at the ILT20 Season 5, recognising a team or individual who best reflects the game's values during the tournament, which begins in the UAE on November 21. The award will be presented at the end of the competition on December 20, marking the first such recognition at the six-team T20 league. MCC, the guardian of cricket's Laws, will work with the tournament organisers to promote sportsmanship and fair play among players. The partnership is part of MCC's wider effort to promote the Spirit of Cricket across the game. The Club has previously worked with ICC Europe to present similar awards at three men's sub-regional World Cup qualification events earlier this year. Rob Lynch, MCC's Director of Cricket and Operations, said franchise leagues could play an important role in setting standards for player behaviour. “MCC sees franchise leagues as the standard-bearers for playing the game in the right way – playing hard but playing fair and with a smile on your face,” Lynch said. He added that the competitive nature of franchise cricket, where international team-mates often face each other, could help improve conduct across the sport. Mike Fordham, Interim Chief Operating Officer of the ILT20, said the partnership aligned with the league's emphasis on sporting values. He also pointed to the participation of players from 19 cricketing nations across its six franchises this season. “The tournament has always been hugely competitive with top quality cricket on display. Our matches have always been played in the right spirit with cricket’s traditional sporting values remaining at the forefront,” Fordham said. Season 5 will run from November 21 to December 20, with matches scheduled at the Sheikh Zayed Cricket Stadium in Abu Dhabi, Dubai International Stadium and Sharjah Cricket Stadium. Defending champions Desert Vipers will be joined by Gulf Giants, MI Emirates, Dubai Capitals, Abu Dhabi Knight Riders and Sharjah Warriorz in the 34-match competition. Previous winners include Gulf Giants, MI Emirates and Dubai Capitals. The new recognition will be separate from the main MCC Spirit of Cricket Award, established by MCC and the BBC in 2013 in honour of Christopher Martin-Jenkins.

sports.title: Chelsea right-back Malo Gusto open to January transfer
sports.description: Chelsea right-back Malo Gusto open to January transfer Chelsea right-back Malo Gusto (23) is open to leaving Chelsea in the January transfer window, according to the BBC . The France international is far from being a guaranteed starter in West London. Since Xabi Alonso’s appointment at Chelsea FC, Gusto’s playign time has dramatically decreased. Despite Reece James’ injury, the former Olympique Lyonnais Academy graduate only started three Premier League games, the last of which dating back to two months ago. The BBC reports that Gusto is set to assess his options before the January transfer window, as he lost his place to Josh Acheampong at right-back. Chelsea were reportedly open to selling the France international right-back – currently at Clairefontaine with Zinédine Zidane’s squad – in exchange for a €85m transfer fee. The player reportedly agreed to join Manchester City at the time , where he would have reunited with former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca. sports.title: Robert Horry Rips Walker Kessler’s Offensive Game: “Guys In Elementary Got Better Post Moves Than Him”
sports.description: Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers have the NBA’s best record at 10-2, and new arrival Walker Kessler has played his part in their early success. Kessler has impressed on defense, and former Laker Robert Horry likes what he has seen from the big man on that end of the floor. What Horry, who won three titles with the Lakers, doesn’t like, though, is Kessler’s offensive game, and he urged him to improve on the Big Shot Bob Podcast . “You know what’s really scary about Walker Kessler?” Horry said. “Hey, I know guys in elementary got better post moves than him. He got no post moves, man. I’m like, who is teaching this dude any post moves? You’re seven f***ing feet tall. Get you a little jump hook, man. You don’t have to dunk everything.” Kessler really doesn’t have a reliable post move. The 25-year-old is primarily a rim-runner, and if you are good at that next to Luka Doncic , you’ll score some points. Kessler is averaging 14.9 points, 10.8 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 1.3 steals, and 2.3 blocks per game for the Lakers in 2026-27. Over 60 percent of his field goal attempts have been within three feet of the basket, and only 1.8 percent have come from beyond 10 feet. Now, Kessler showed off some range in the 2025-26 season for the Utah Jazz . He went 6-8 from three in five games before needing season-ending shoulder surgery. So, when the Lakers acquired Kessler, the No. 22 pick in the 2022 NBA Draft, from the Jazz in the summer, the expectation was that he’d be a threat from beyond the arc. He even shared that head coach JJ Redick wanted him to shoot more threes , but he hasn’t even attempted a single one through 12 games. “I don’t even think he wants to score ’cause I’ve seen him get offensive rebounds and kick that b***h out instead of crunching that b***h,” Horry said. “… I’m like, dude, you 7 ft tall. Get you a power dribble. Go up and dunk that b***h too. Like [Shaquille O’Neal], you monkey dunk that b***h. That’s what he said. That’s what Shaq used to say. So dunk on somebody and then just move on. “That’s what I want him to do and stop kicking that b***h out ’cause you don’t get no plays ran for you,” Horry added. Now, teams like the player who gets the offensive rebound to kick it out for an open three. That could well be the case here, but we don’t know for sure. While Kessler isn’t the perfect offensive center, that wasn’t why the Lakers gave him a four-year, $130 million contract and gave up two first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps to the Jazz. They wanted a rim runner and a defensive anchor, and he is just that. “He’s a great shot blocker,” Horry said. “And the thing I like about Kessler the best is he goes after everything. And even though he’s gotten dunked on a couple times, he don’t give a s***… He’s still going to go out and try to block. sports.title: Top 2027 recruit Amaya Manuel commits to Tennessee
sports.description: Top 2027 recruit Amaya Manuel has committed to Tennessee , she announced. The 5-8 point guard from Saint Louis (MO) Lift For Life Academy chose the Lady Vols over programs including Missouri and Arkansas. “Definitely a family type of environment,” she previously told Rivals of factors she was considering. “I want to do a lot of team bonding and stuff. I really want to have a good relationship with all the teammates and all my coaches. I also want a program that’s big on development for each player. You know, let me do what I what I can do, not limiting me, but making me better.” Tennessee earned the last official visit and the commitment. The Lady Vols are getting a strong point guard in Manuel. “My biggest strength is definitely driving,” she said. “I just came back from my ACL injury in November, so I’m just now coming back, but I’ve always been able to drive and be aggressive. I’m trying to get back to that. I still think that’s my strength, but I need to get better at that now.” Manuel marks Tennessee’s second commitment in the 2027 class after adding versatile wing Maci Pringle.

sports.title: JJ Gabriel set to sign Real Madrid contract by early next week – report
sports.description: JJ Gabriel set to sign Real Madrid contract by early next week – report Real Madrid are expected to complete the signing of Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel by the beginning of next week, with the 16-year-old’s move to the Spanish capital approaching its final stages. According to journalist Ben Fernandes Santos , the agreement is close to being finalised, with the teenager having made his preference clear to the European clubs interested in securing his signature. It is to be noted that Gabriel attracted attention across Europe following his decision to leave Manchester United in September. Real Madrid, after tough negotiations and a fight with other suitors, emerged as his preferred destination, with Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain among the clubs previously linked with the highly-rated forward. Manchester United fail to convince JJ Gabriel to stay Manchester United reportedly made several attempts to change Gabriel’s mind, with club executives and manager Michael Carrick holding discussions with the player and his representatives. Real Madrid could announce JJ Gabriel’s signing by next week. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) However, those efforts did not alter his intention to pursue a move to Real Madrid. The teenager requested to leave United in September and has since been training independently in Spain while his future is being resolved. His decision became clearer when he was asked to choose between Barcelona and Real Madrid . “Obviously, Real Madrid,” he said. As reported before, Real Madrid had reached a verbal agreement with the teenager and were confident of signing him. However, formal club-to-club negotiations had not yet taken place until a few weeks back. Real Madrid have a clear development plan Real Madrid have won the race for JJ Gabriel. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) Real Madrid are understood to want Gabriel to begin his development with Castilla , allowing him to experience senior football while remaining close to the first-team environment. The Spanish club believe their pathway offers an attractive opportunity for the teenager to progress towards the senior squad. His representative, Ali Barat, has been involved in discussions over the move, while reports have also suggested that Jose Mourinho played a role in convincing Gabriel that Madrid would be the right destination. All in all, Real Madrid are set to sign the highly-rated teenager, and the official announcement could be arriving soon.

The top spot changed hands, while Miami dropped six places to No. 7 despite losing by only a touchdown. This week’s list shows massive movement across the board, with no team staying in the same position as last week. Georgia, Notre Dame, and the Bruins all saw their stock rise significantly following recent results. UCLA moved up four spots to No. 4 after a 34-20 victory over Minnesota. Miles Russell isn’t just the unquestioned top-ranked player in the Class of 2027 as the week-long early signing period starts Wednesday; the 18-year-old from Jacksonville Beach, Florida, might be the best college prospect in over a decade. He will sign with the Florida State Seminoles, who also have the No. 1 class, which includes top European recruit Edwin Askerfors, Tiger Woods’ son Charlie Woods and instate product Kaden Puranik. The Bruins and Longhorns are the only programs to ink a pair of top-10 signings while the Demon Deacons will bring in No. 1 Amelia Zalsman as an early enrollee this spring. sports.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
sports.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. sports.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
sports.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. sports.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
sports.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame.
